symptom: canon.Reconcile was 23 s of a 77 s settled re-run of 600 pages, about 38 ms for each rebuilt page compared with its stored unit (ako/mxcli#2160)
cause: Reconcile is a row of steps from bytes to bytes - carry translations, transplant ids, carry PersistentIds, carry what MDL cannot state, compare - and each parses both documents for itself: twelve whole-document parses for one write. Five of them served steps that either only read the stored document or did not need a tree at all: the id substitution parsed the document before and after patching to read its ids, the PersistentId carry parsed both documents to find that a page has no PersistentId, and the transplant and the final comparison each parsed the stored document
file: modelsdk/canon/identity.go (Reconcile, parseStored, equalToStored, reconcileInPasses), modelsdk/canon/transplant.go (transplantIDs, idMappingWith, elementIDSetOf), modelsdk/canon/persistentid.go (persistentIDElement), modelsdk/canon/canon.go (digestOfDoc)
insight: The obvious change - parse each document once and hand the trees to every step - is unsafe here, and reading the steps showed why before any test did: the translation carry and the unexpressed carry copy parts of the stored tree into the new one, so a shared stored tree could be changed under the steps after them, and the new document changes between steps. Only the steps that provably just read the stored document share its parse (the transplant's pairing and the final digest); the carries keep a parse of their own. The other two savings need no tree: the ids are read off the raw bytes, and a document that does not contain the bytes of a binary PersistentId element has nothing to carry. Twelve parses become seven. The old Reconcile is kept verbatim as reconcileInPasses and compared byte for byte, with the verdict, on every PedApp unit against itself, a rebuild with new ids, rebuilds with properties left out, and the reverse: 2,214 comparisons. The fixture has no workflow, so the PersistentId path was unexercised on both sides; a workflow-shaped pair is compared separately, and always skipping the carry fails three tests. A first version of that control did not compile (the mutation left an import unused) and printed nothing, which reads like a pass: a control has to be seen to fail. End to end, a script changing all 600 pages run with the old and the new binary leaves 1,719 byte-identical units, 600 of which differ from before the run. Measured: settled page re-run 74.3 s -> 61.6 s, changed-pages run 72.1 s -> 65.6 s.
